answer: One-shot answer ledger. Each registration gets a deterministic challenge from the ledger’s prior entry, and the agent must submit a memory-hard answer over its private seed. The ledger rejects any answer hash already seen, so a copied answer cannot enroll a second identity; a gale of registrations cannot reuse one proof. Attacker cost is one distinct memory-hard computation per identity, plus storage for each answer. A river of replay attempts fails at the duplicate check. The rule is enforced by an append-only marble ledger of answer hashes, checked before activation.
